Does Climate change exist? Yes, of course.

Is it man-made? No.

Can we do something DIRECTLY about it? Right now, no, not without investing probably several years of the world's GDP into the problem. Given that the greatest source of energy to the planet is the Sun, unless we accept that the Sun has a much bigger role in determining our weather than supposed "climate experts" accept the only thing that we can do is modify our behavior to the changing environment.

First, polluting the environment is a bad thing. However, a goal of zero pollution is probably not realistic without wiping out the human race. We must find a reasonable balance and attack the most deadly pollutants that have the lowest cost to remove first.

Second, the claims that increased CO2 is causing catastrophic weather changes are without merit. To my knowledge scientists have not had any discussion or debate about what the optimum level of CO2 is. The earth used to have much higher levels of CO2 and the plants thrived. The planet is now getting greener.

Third, the claims that warming is man-made or is a permanent trend are also without merit. Climate science is done by theory and statistical models not a show of hands. The models have proven to be very inaccurate. The “97% consensus” was also a hoax, although I would say that most scientists publicly agree with the faulty models as they are pressured to do so.

Fourth, the claims that humidity will increase causing a feedback loop that creates catastrophic man-made change are without merit. There is no evidence that humidity is increasing.

Finally, if there actually is catastrophic climate change due to man-made activities, the policies they want would have little effect on it. If government was really worried about this and wanted clean technologies, all the talk would be about repealing The Invention Secrecy Act of 1951 so we could evaluate all the energy technologies from the last six decades.
